Trading Post Operations Manual
Data verified on LIVE Build: Alpha 4.10.1

1. Terminal Basics
Every commodity terminal enforces local supply and demand curves independently. When a terminal shows insufficient buy capacity, the terminal has hit demand saturation for that commodity and will refuse further sell orders until its inventory refresh ticks restore headroom.

DEMAND SATURATION MECHANICS
Demand saturation occurs when cumulative sell volume at a single terminal exceeds its rolling capacity window. Selling in smaller batches across multiple inventory refresh ticks avoids triggering a hard refusal. Prices depress sharply once saturation begins.

2. Route Planning
Compare two terminals separated by several jumps and check the cluster multiplier applied to bulk hauling missions before committing cargo space. A low cluster multiplier rarely offsets fuel and time cost.

3. Inventory Refresh Timing
Inventory refresh ticks run on a fixed real-time interval per terminal. Waiting one additional tick before re-selling is usually enough to clear a demand saturation flag.
